appraisal_events.evidence: Albertine avait dépouillé... ses différents caractères d'humanité qui m'avaient déçu... Elle n'était plus animée que de la vie inconsciente des végétaux... j'avais cette impression de la posséder tout entière que je n'avais pas quand elle était réveillée. Sa vie m'était soumise.
appraisal_events.explanation: Watching her sleep, the narrator recasts Albertine as an unconscious, plant-like body stripped of the human traits (and the escaping selfhood) that had disappointed him; her personhood is narratively reduced to passive, possessed matter, even as the narrator frames this transformation as an object of tender love rather than contempt.

status_effects.explanation: Reduced to unconscious, vegetal, 'captive' status, she loses the autonomous self ('son moi') that otherwise escapes through unspoken thought and gaze when awake.
The narrator gains, in this same movement, a sense of total possession and inner completeness over Albertine that he lacks when she is awake and he must 'live at the surface of himself.'

ambiguities: The narrator's possessive framing of the sleeping Albertine ('la charmante captive', reduced to plant-like passivity) is presented affectionately and without explicit narratorial irony, so it is treated as endorsed rather than ironized; a more skeptical reading of this asymmetry (his gain built on her unconsciousness and loss of selfhood) is possible but not clearly staged by the passage itself.
